title: Work, Energy and Power

cards.h: The universe's most useful bank account
cards.b:
Energy is the one quantity physicists trust above all. It can change form, from a falling stone's motion to heat, from sunlight to electricity, but the total never changes.

That rule lets you solve problems that Newton's laws would make painful. You do not need to track every force along a roller coaster; you only need to know where it starts and ends.

In physics, work is done when a force moves something.

Work

W = F x d x cos(theta)

Here theta is the angle between force and motion. The unit is the joule (J): one newton pushing through one metre.

Holding a heavy bag still does no work in this sense, since nothing moves. Carrying it level also does no work on the bag, because your upward force is at right angles to the motion (cos 90 = 0). Lifting it does work.

cards.h: Kinetic energy: the energy of motion
cards.b:
Kinetic energy

KE = (1/2) m v squared

Note the square. Double your speed and the energy goes up four times. That is why a car crash at 100 km/h is far worse than at 50 km/h, and why stopping distances grow so fast.

The work-energy theorem: the net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy.

Lift a mass m to height h and you store energy in the gravitational field:

Gravitational PE

PE = m g h

Stretch a spring, compress a gas, separate two charges: all store potential energy. Release it and it turns back into motion.

A force like gravity, where the work done depends only on start and end points, is called conservative.

If only conservative forces act, KE + PE stays constant. A ball rolling down a hill trades height for speed.

With friction, mechanical energy appears to vanish, but it has turned into heat. Count the heat and the total is still the same. This is the law of conservation of energy.

Power

P = W / t

Power is work done per second. The unit is the watt: one joule per second. A 100 W bulb uses 100 J every second. One horsepower is about 746 W.

Your electricity bill counts in kilowatt-hours (kWh). One kWh is 1000 W for 3600 s, which is 3.6 million joules. That is one 'unit' of electricity.

cards.h: A 2 kg stone dropped from 5 m
cards.b:
PE at the top: m g h = 2 x 9.8 x 5 = 98 J.

Just before landing all of it is KE: (1/2) x 2 x v squared = 98, so v squared = 98 and v is about 9.9 m/s.

Notice the mass cancels: v = square root of (2 g h) for any stone. Compare with the motion equation v squared = 2 g h. Same answer, easier route.

• Energy is 'used up'. It is converted, not destroyed. A phone charger just moves energy around and wastes some as heat.
  • Work is any effort. In physics, no motion along the force, no work.
  • Power equals energy. A weak motor can lift a heavy load over a long time; a strong one does it faster. Same energy, different power.

Hydroelectric dams are conservation of energy in action: water stored high (PE) falls through turbines (KE) and spins generators. The Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej, completed in the early 1960s, is among India's tallest gravity dams, and Jawaharlal Nehru called such dams the 'temples of modern India'.

Every Indian household bill is in kWh, the same 3.6 million joules in the example above. When you use a 1000 W heater for an hour, you pay for exactly one unit.

• Work W = F d cos(theta), measured in joules.
  • KE = (1/2) m v squared; PE = m g h.
  • Total energy is conserved; friction turns it to heat.
  • Power = work / time, in watts. 1 kWh = 3.6 million J.

Think about it

1. Why does doubling a car's speed quadruple its braking distance?
2. A roller coaster's second hill is never taller than the first. Why?
